title: v1-chat-parameter-shim-and-stream-protocol-tool-output-envelope
author: Evan Morales
description:
Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions surface expect stable streaming behavior, predictable stop/logprob semantics, and tool/function-calling output that is reliably parseable across latency spikes and server-side buffering. This PR implements a compact parameter shim that maps common /v1 parameters into Redwood's internal serving options, smooths stop-probability mass handling so stop arrays and stop strings behave consistently, and introduces a lightweight streaming envelope for tool/function outputs to avoid truncated or interleaved JSON fragments when backpressure or retries occur.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds an API shim (go/internal/api/v1shim.go) that normalizes v1 fields: "messages", "temperature", "top_p", "stop" (string|array), "max_tokens", and the function-calling keys into our canonical options bag. The shim preserves role aliases (e.g., "assistant"/"system" variants) and emits warnings to the debug logs when ambiguous fields are used.
- Introduces stop-weight smoothing logic: when a stop array is provided, we reallocate conditional token probabilities at the framing layer to avoid overcounting overlapping stop sequences (reduces spurious partial-stop tokens and aligns emitted stop token logprobs with user expectations). This is implemented in runtime/stream/stop_normalizer.go.
- Streaming protocol improvements: runtime/stream/framer.go and runtime/stream/backpressure.go implement a sentinel-and-fence pattern. A small sentinel token (0xEE marker) is injected at function-call/JSON-tool boundaries during streaming; a matching fence ensures that if the connection or server interrupts mid-fragment we either retry that fragment or emit a clearly delimited partial payload marker the client can detect and recover from.
- Tool/function output envelope: runtime/codec/tool_envelope.go wraps tool outputs with a compact header containing origin metadata (tool id, schema version, byte-length) and a CRC. This prevents accidental merging of two adjacent JSON blobs in high-throughput streaming scenarios and makes the SDK recovery code simpler.
- Tests and docs: added unit tests (api/openai_compat/translator_test.go), integration tests that simulate partial TCP writes, and docs (docs/openai-compat.md) describing the shim and best practices for migration. Also included a Python example (sdk/python/openai_compat_example.py) showing how to use the shim and detect envelope boundaries.

Checklist: 
- [x] Param shim implementation
- [x] Stop-weight smoothing algorithm and tests
- [x] Streaming sentinel/fence to prevent truncated JSON merge
- [x] Envelope CRC and header for tool outputs
- [x] Integration tests that simulate backpressure and partial writes
- [x] Docs and example updated
- [x] Addressed security review concerns about header metadata exposure

Backward compatibility notes: The shim is additive and only activates for requests routed to the openai-compat adapter. Existing native Redwood API calls are unaffected. The streaming sentinel is negotiated per-connection via the handshake; endpoints that opt out will continue to use the legacy framing.

Performance/impact: Microbenchmarks show sub-1% median latency impact on steady-state single-request flows and a 6-9% reduction in malformed tool-output incidents under synthetic high-concurrency streaming load. Production dogfood on a subset of Hosted traffic ran for 48 hours with no SLA regressions.

Deployment plan: Feature gated behind a runtime flag and the openai-compat adapter. Canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and monitoring dashboards added to Console: metric names included in docs.

Related work: ENG-1427 is the upstream spec for v1 param mapping; SUP-472 tracked a customer incident that surfaced the truncated-json issue.

release_notes: Adds an OpenAI /v1 chat compatibility shim that normalizes parameters, stabilizes streaming for function/tool outputs by introducing a minimal envelope + sentinel protocol, and aligns stop/logprob semantics for stop arrays. Backward compatible and feature-gated behind the openai-compat adapter.
